rejected.title: Half-life and radiocarbon dating
card: Half-life is the time it takes for half of the unstable atoms in a sample to decay. After one half-life, half remain. After two, a quarter remain.
Living things take in carbon, including a small share of unstable carbon-14, while they are alive. When they die, they stop taking it in.
Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,700 years. Measuring how much is left in charcoal, bone or shell shows how long ago the living thing died.
Radiocarbon dating has dated many First Peoples' campsites and burials in Australia. It works back to about 50,000 years, so older sites need other methods.
rejected.remember: Each half-life halves the unstable atoms left, so less carbon-14 means an older sample.

a.q: A sample starts with 800 unstable atoms, and its half-life is 2 hours. How many unstable atoms are left after 6 hours?
a.why: Six hours is three half-lives, so 800 halves to 400, then 200, then 100. No atoms would mean the same number decays each time, but each half-life halves what is left.

b.q: Charcoal from an old campsite has a quarter of the carbon-14 that living wood has. About how long ago did the tree it came from die?
b.why: A quarter left means two half-lives have passed, and 2 × 5,700 = 11,400 years. About 5,700 years would leave half, not a quarter.
b.clue: How many halvings turn the whole amount into a quarter?

version.title: Half-life and radiocarbon dating
card: Half-life is the time it takes for half of the unstable atoms in a sample to decay. After one half-life, half are left. After two, a quarter are left.
Living things take in carbon, including a tiny share of unstable carbon-14, while they are alive. When they die, they take in no more, and their carbon-14 slowly decays.
Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,700 years. Comparing the carbon-14 left in charcoal, bone or shell with a living sample shows how long ago it died.
Radiocarbon dating has dated many First Peoples' campsites and burials in Australia. It works up to about 50,000 years ago, so older sites need other dating methods.
version.remember: Less carbon-14 left means more half-lives have passed, so the sample is older.

a.q: A sample has 1,200 unstable atoms, and its half-life is 3 days. How many unstable atoms are left after 9 days?
a.why: Nine days is three half-lives: 1,200 halves to 600, then 300, then 150. 400 comes from dividing by 3, but each half-life halves what is left.
a.clue: Halve it once for each half-life.

b.q: A shell from an old campsite has one eighth of the carbon-14 that a living shell has. About how long ago did it die?
b.why: One eighth left means three half-lives: a half, a quarter, then an eighth. 3 × 5,700 = 17,100 years. 45,600 comes from multiplying by 8, but each half-life halves what is left, so an eighth takes only three.
b.clue: How many halvings turn the whole into an eighth?
